summary: Say the counting numbers in order to 10, and keep going past 10.
Start to recognize some written numbers and try writing a few of them.
Link numbers to amounts: count one by one, count out a given number to 10, see up to 5 at a glance.
Count up to 10 things one by one to answer how many there are.
Tell whether a group of up to 5 has more, fewer or the same as another, by matching or counting.
Say which one is first and which one is last in a line or an order.
See adding as putting groups together and subtracting as taking some away, using objects.
Solve simple adding and taking-away story problems with help from an adult.
Add by joining two groups of objects and counting how many there are now.
Copy, make up and continue simple repeating patterns with real objects.
With help, name what can be measured about a thing, such as how long or how heavy it is.
Compare sizes with words like longer, heavier or bigger, and read simple tables and graphs.
Sort objects into groups by color, size or shape, then count each group up to 5.
Name the shapes of things nearby and say where they are: over, under, inside, in front, behind.
Name basic shapes correctly whatever their size or which way they are turned.
Sort flat shapes and solid shapes, and objects shaped like them, into groups.
Compare flat and solid shapes of different sizes and say how they are alike and different.
Build shapes out of parts, such as sticks joined with clay balls.
With help, put small shapes together to make a bigger one, like two triangles into a rectangle.
